influenceLayers.title: TCM Framework
paragraphs:
In Traditional Chinese Medicine, the Lung (Fei) governs the skin and Wei Qi—the protective electromagnetic boundary between self and world. The Spleen (Pi)
governs transportation and transformation—the ability to process food, experiences, and emotions into usable energy and waste.
When you have been chronically exposed to stress, conflict, or emotional invasion—without the ability to set boundaries—the Lung's Wei Qi becomes deficient. The
protective barrier weakens. Simultaneously, the Spleen, overwhelmed by worry and rumination, fails to transform dampness. This dampness combines with wind
(stress) and heat (suppressed anger) to create a skin that is dry, inflamed, and unbearably itchy.
Eczema is not a skin condition. It is the physical manifestation of a boundary that has been breached so many times it no longer knows how to hold. The itch is the
body's way of saying "I am being invaded. I need to protect myself. I need to scratch away what is touching me."

influenceLayers.title: Clinical Cascade (Chronic Stress → Barrier Dysfunction → Inflammatory Response)
paragraphs:
Chronic psychological stress disrupts the skin barrier by elevating cortisol and suppressing the production of ceramides and filaggrin—proteins essential for skin

of Dermatology confirms that stress is a primary trigger for eczema flares, with 80% of patients reporting symptom onset during high-stress periods.

influenceLayers.title: TCM Framework
paragraphs:
In Traditional Chinese Medicine, the Liver (Gan) stores the Blood and governs the smooth flow of Qi. The Liver's emotion is anger—specifically, frustrated, stuck,
unexpressed rage. The Spleen (Pi) governs the transformation and transportation of nutrients and Blood. When Qi stagnates, Blood congeals. When Blood congeals,
it forms masses.
The mole is not a random collection of pigment cells. It is the physical manifestation of stuck emotional material. It is the body's way of saying "something got stuck
here. Something wasn't processed. Something wasn't released." The mole is the record. It is the proof of the moment when energy stopped flowing. It is the bookmark
in the book of your life, marking the chapter where something didn't move through.

influenceLayers.title: Jungian Shadow
paragraphs:
You have suppressed the archetype of the Movable One—the part that knows how to adapt, how to shift, how to change. Somewhere early, you learned that change
was dangerous. That letting go meant losing. That staying the same was safety. Your shadow self—the one who wants to move, to grow, to transform—has been
locked in the basement.
But the body does not forget. The cells that should have moved, shifted, and transformed have stayed. They have become fixed. They have become marks. The mole
is the permanent reminder of the moment you decided it was safer to stay than to grow. It is the marker of the choice to remain the same.
